report.answer: An orange basketball is dropped from rest and falls straight down onto a wooden floor. The fall fits free-fall projectile motion with no detectable air drag, giving Earth gravity, and the ball does not bounce back up in the 2 s clip — it stops at the floor.
assumptions: fall is vertical in a plane facing the camera
scale from basketball itself, diameter 0.24 m +/-0.01 m at same depth as motion

forks.label: vacuum drop
forks.why: drag model already decisively rejected; vacuum would look identical

forks.label: bouncy floor
forks.why: see how high a live basketball would rebound

forks.label: Moon drop
forks.why: same 2.2 m drop would take ~1.65x longer to fall

derived.name: terminal_velocity
derived.desc: sqrt(g/b): speed at which drag balances gravity (null if b <= 0)

derived.name: omega
derived.desc: angular frequency of the damped oscillation

derived.name: damping_time
derived.desc: 1/gamma: amplitude e-folding time (null if not damped)

derived.name: Q
derived.desc: quality factor omega_n / (2 gamma) (null if not damped)
